description: How the kings of mobile fell (2006–2026). A dramatic market-share race: Nokia and BlackBerry collapse after the iPhone’s rise, Samsung and Apple dominate, and Huawei rockets — then gets cut down by sanctions. This timeline shows the winner-takes-most shift that remade the phone business.
youtube_description: From the pre-iPhone era to the sanction-era shakeout: this visualization races 20 years of market share and tells one impossible-sounding story — how two giants (Nokia, BlackBerry) went from reigning the handset world to single-digit — while newcomers and survivors (Apple, Samsung) carved up the market. Notice Huawei’s meteoric rise through the 2010s and the brutal fall after 2019 U.S. restrictions that cut it off from western chip supplies. Sources: industry shipment and market-share reports (IDC/Strategy Analytics/Counterpoint) and public company disclosures.
